significance.justification: A verified-true result would establish that a separable “surface-trigger shortcut” directly activates refusal execution on benign trigger-bearing prompts, while harmfulness belief drives justified refusals, and that selectively suppressing the former preserves the latter; this is a form-(ii) causal decomposition rather than a quantitative law. It establishes both a behavioral phenomenon and a mechanism, splitting two refusal outcomes between independently manipulable contributors and thereby constraining explanations and mitigation choices more strongly than the standard single refusal-direction account exemplified by Arditi et al., “Refusal in Language Models Is Mediated by a Single Direction” (2024). The branches are distinguishable: a negative result would rule out the claimed shortcut as the dominant separable cause of over-refusal, although the compound wording would not by itself identify which alternative mechanism is responsible. Topic substitution fails—the broad safety-and-interpretability topic alone would not earn this score; the specific two-pathway decomposition and differential consequences for over-refusal versus genuine safety support the elevation above the topic median.

reach.justification: The concrete handle is the “trigger-salience component of the residual stream” and the associated “training-free intervention that ablates only” that component while preserving harmfulness belief. This is an ex-ante inference-time control because it acts before the refusal or unsafe compliance is produced, giving deployers a usable action window rather than merely explaining an observed failure. Re-extraction on a new model would still require calibration, but the conclusion predicts the categorical relation to recover—trigger-path dominance on benign-with-trigger cases and harmfulness-path dominance on genuinely harmful cases—rather than numerical effect sizes; the hypothesis speaks broadly of “LLM over-refusals,” though its asserted cross-architecture scope is not sharply bounded. The handle could be used by researchers and practitioners who audit or ship safety-aligned models, and the topic-substitution check fails because generic mechanistic safety supplies neither this selective intervention nor its promised refusal/safety separation.
